tagline: We develop technology that transforms the future
hero_kpi_rationale: Orders received are the primary indicator of future demand in Atlas Copco's industrial model, reflecting the health of customer investments in industrial equipment and sustainable solutions, a key driver of its structural growth.

kpis.name: Orders received
kpis.explanation: Total value of new incoming orders during the year.
kpis.description: Orders received are a key indicator of future demand, particularly important in industrial sectors where sales cycles are long.
kpis.signal: Slight decline in orders in 2025, indicating a moderate slowdown in industrial demand.

kpis.name: Revenues
kpis.explanation: Total group revenue for the year.
kpis.description: Revenues reflect the group's overall commercial performance, impacted by volumes and pricing.
kpis.signal: Revenues declining in 2025, reflecting a challenging industrial environment.

kpis.name: EBITDA
kpis.explanation: Earnings before interest, taxes, depreciation, and amortization.
kpis.description: EBITDA reflects the operational ability to generate profits before financial and accounting charges.
kpis.signal: EBITDA declining, reflecting pressure on volumes and negative operating leverage.

kpis.name: EBITDA Margin
kpis.explanation: EBITDA expressed as a percentage of revenues.
kpis.description: EBITDA margin reflects operational efficiency and the ability to maintain profitability amid market pressures.
kpis.signal: EBITDA margin slightly compressed despite a difficult environment, indicating strong cost control.

kpis.name: Op Margin
kpis.description: Operating margin measures profitability after operating expenses, including R&D and marketing.
kpis.signal: Operating margin compression in 2025, reflecting the impact of lower volumes on fixed costs.

kpis.name: EBITA
kpis.explanation: Earnings before interest, taxes, and amortization of intangible assets related to acquisitions.
kpis.description: EBITA is a key performance indicator, excluding acquisition-related amortization to better reflect underlying performance.
kpis.signal: EBITA declining significantly, reflecting pressure on fixed costs and lower volumes.

kpis.name: Operating cash flow
kpis.explanation: Cash generated from the company's core business activities (cash flow post-investments).
kpis.description: Operating cash flow shows the company's ability to generate cash from operations after investments.
kpis.signal: Operating cash flow declining notably, reflecting pressure on profitability and potentially on working capital.

kpis.name: EBITA Margin
kpis.explanation: EBITA expressed as a percentage of revenues.
kpis.description: EBITA margin reflects operational profitability excluding acquisition amortization, a key metric for Atlas Copco.
kpis.signal: EBITA margin under pressure, reflecting operating deleveraging due to lower volumes.

kpis.name: ROCE
kpis.explanation: Measures how efficiently the company uses its capital to generate profits.
kpis.description: ROCE is a key performance indicator to assess value creation relative to invested capital.
kpis.signal: ROCE declining significantly, reflecting margin compression and potentially higher capital…

risks.title: Quality and reliability of sustainability data
risks.score_rationale: Risk positioned in the central section of the sustainability report, with moderate language ('could be materially different'); stable trend but reinforced by the 2025 thematic audit identifying gaps; regulatory category with high weight due to CSRD/ESRS obligations.

risks.title: Compliance with CSRD requirements and ESRS standards
risks.score_rationale: Risk mentioned at the beginning of the section on preparation basis, with factual but binding language; increasing trend as 2025 is the first year of mandatory ESRS reporting for the group; regulatory category with high weight.

risks.title: Gaps in sustainable reporting governance
risks.score_rationale: Risk identified in the middle of the report, with direct language signaling actual gaps ('corrective actions have been implemented to address the identified gaps'); increasing trend as the 2025 internal audit formally identified shortcomings; reputational category with moderate weight.

risks.title: Risks related to responsible AI use and cybersecurity
risks.score_rationale: Risk mentioned in the 2025 Code of Conduct update, signaling a new and growing concern; preventive language but integrated into a core governance document; emerging trend; cybersecurity category with high weight according to analysis criteria.

risks.title: Late integration of acquisitions into reporting scope
risks.score_rationale: Risk positioned at the end of the consolidation scope section, with descriptive and factual language; stable trend linked to the group's ongoing acquisition strategy; industrial category with moderate weight, but direct impact on the reliability of published data.

risks.title: Human rights risks in the value chain
risks.score_rationale: Risk mentioned in the central section of the sustainability report with explicit reference to binding international frameworks (UN, OECD); strengthened due diligence language; stable trend but increasing regulatory framework in Europe; regulatory category with high weight.

risks.title: Decentralization and heterogeneity of operational controls
risks.score_rationale: Risk mentioned at the beginning of the organizational structure section, with neutral language but highlighting dependence on local entities; stable trend linked to the group's historical decentralized model; industrial category with moderate weight, with impact on consistency of data and practices.

ai_positioning.summary: Atlas Copco does not appear as a leader in generative AI, but is progressively integrating digital and automation technologies into its industrial solutions. The focus is on efficiency, sustainability, and equipment connectivity.
evidence: No mention of generative AI or language models in the report.
Focus on automation, digitalization, and connected solutions.
No references to AI APIs, AI deals, or AI adoption metrics.
